items.streamTitle: Sequential working memory was represented in neural subspaces, without detectable replay
items.streamSummary: Human MEG decoding identified item-position-specific neural subspaces and no detectable sequential replay during retention. The null is bounded by the task and measurement methods.
items.attribution: Santo-Angles et al. — Nature Communications

items.streamTitle: Anti-extremist statements were processed faster in two Indian priming experiments
items.streamSummary: Two experiments found faster, more accurate responses to anti-Naxalite than pro-Naxalite statements. Response speed and agreement do not establish persuasion or the mechanism behind the difference.
items.attribution: Kumar et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Dynamic-network theorem identified conditions favoring modeled cooperation
items.streamSummary: A new evolutionary-game theorem reduced network effects to three coefficients and found some changing core–periphery structures favored modeled prosociality. Exogenous network dynamics and no human validation bound the result.
items.attribution: Zhang et al. — Nature Computational Science

items.streamTitle: Peer-rejection brain responses predicted some later mood outcomes in adolescents
items.streamSummary: EEG responses in 179 adolescents were associated with subsequent mood and, among 37 with current depression, symptom severity. This is prospective observational evidence, not causal identification.
items.attribution: Kim et al. — NPP—Digital Psychiatry and Neuroscience

items.streamTitle: Fabricated election polling entered major aggregation pipelines before being exposed
items.streamSummary: FiftyPlusOne identified anomalies in Wedgewood survey data, and the firm admitted fabrication on October 20. Aggregators withdrew polls, but downstream effects on voters or campaigns are not established.
items.attribution: Radcliffe, Morris and Burton — FiftyPlusOne original investigation

items.streamTitle: Nine AI persuasion evaluations disagreed substantially on model rankings
items.streamSummary: Across 15 models, adapted automated persuasion benchmarks showed weak mean rank agreement (rho≈0.25). Differences in task definitions and model refusals limit broad persuasiveness claims.
items.attribution: Dementaviciute, Vaitonyte and De Bie — arXiv preprint

items.streamTitle: Behavioral history helped AI personas, but individual prediction remained weak
items.streamSummary: In an 845-person two-wave panel, demographic and personality personas poorly predicted individual biases; adding earlier choices improved signal to 28% of human test–retest performance. Aggregate similarity overstated fidelity.
items.attribution: Pourtaheri and Zareei — arXiv preprint

items.streamTitle: Phone-image Gaussian splatting enabled lower-cost digital twins with scale limits
items.streamSummary: An eCAADe study compared smartphone-based 3D reconstructions against drone LiDAR across scales. Quality depended strongly on image coverage; XR-training transfer remains untested.
items.attribution: Aman et al. — eCAADe 2026 conference paper

items.streamTitle: Village-randomized media-literacy lessons improved misinformation discernment
items.streamSummary: A 583-village experiment involving roughly 13,600 Indian adolescents found improved health-news discernment, some four-month persistence, transfer to political news, and parent spillovers. The multi-part curriculum limits mechanism attribution.
items.attribution: Amar et al. — American Political Science Review (foundational 2025 field experiment)

items.streamTitle: Attention during search draws on more than working memory
items.streamSummary: A Nature Reviews Psychology synthesis argues that visual search uses flexible target representations, long-term memory, statistical learning, and distractor avoidance, rather than only a working-memory template.
items.attribution: Carlisle and Woodman — Nature Reviews Psychology (review)

items.streamTitle: Causally informed model combines satellite and underwater measurements
items.streamSummary: A new marine-water-quality framework integrates prior structural assumptions with satellite and glider observations. It offers a modeling method, not experimental confirmation of the inferred causal structure.
items.attribution: Hashemi, Mahjouri and Nikoo — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: Sensation seeking and impulsivity showed opposite uncertainty patterns
items.streamSummary: A preregistered task with 527 analyzed adults found sensation-seeking related to greater tolerance of uncertain stimulation, whereas impulsivity related to greater avoidance. These model-based patterns need real-world replication.
items.attribution: Wong et al. — Communications Psychology

items.streamTitle: Partisan economic labels obscured shared preferences in US and Brazil
items.streamSummary: Five studies found cross-party support for elements of a mixed economy despite different capitalist/socialist labels. Showing participants the agreement reduced perceived divides and raised stated openness to out-party policies; voting was not measured.
items.attribution: Woodley and Greene — Nature Communications

items.streamTitle: Knowledge-tracing model improved benchmark prediction, with an F1 exception
items.streamSummary: MEDKT combined behavior history, concept graphs, sequential attention, and modeled forgetting. Three public dataset benchmarks showed small gains on most metrics, while one F1 comparison did not improve.
items.attribution: Zong et al. — Scientific Reports

items.streamTitle: AI patient-simulator pilot found no clear skill advantage over alternatives
items.streamSummary: A multi-stage study evaluated 350 scripted encounters, 155 live student interactions, and a 58-person randomized pilot. Exam gains did not differ significantly by training arm; equivalence was not demonstrated.
items.attribution: Wu et al. — npj Digital Medicine

items.streamTitle: AI and peer feedback improved some feedback-literacy measures in a classroom study
items.streamSummary: Across 126 students in three intact classes, AI and peer feedback coincided with gains on some self-reported feedback-literacy dimensions; the teacher group showed no significant changes. Assignment was not randomized.
items.attribution: Yan and Meng — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Brain-computer interface review puts generalization ahead of peak accuracy
items.streamSummary: A new review argues that neural decoding must be tested across sessions, participants, tasks, hardware, and clinical conditions. High development scores alone do not establish durable clinical use.
items.attribution: Gu et al. — npj Biomedical Innovations (review)

items.streamTitle: Army AI supplier announced a $700 million enterprise contract ceiling
items.streamSummary: Striveworks said its enterprise agreement grew tenfold and would support more Army AI deployments. The headline figure is a ceiling, not funds spent or independently verified mission improvement.
items.attribution: Striveworks — company announcement, October 22

items.streamTitle: UNIDIR starts a 2026–27 AI security lexicon initiative
items.streamSummary: UNIDIR outlined a multidisciplinary effort to clarify AI security terminology for policymakers, including contested definitions. The October 23 event and plan are not evidence that agreement or adoption has occurred.
items.attribution: UNIDIR — official AI security lexicon event

items.streamTitle: Emergency managers ranked organizational context as central to AI adoption
items.streamSummary: Expert interviews and fuzzy DEMATEL analysis in China identified contextual and decision-process barriers to generative-AI adoption in crises. The findings are perceived relationships, not demonstrated effects.
items.attribution: Fei, Sun and Sun — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: More policy coverage tracked public participation, not necessarily favorable sentiment
items.streamSummary: Across 232 Chinese cities, talent-policy media attention had a nonlinear association with a combined response index, while sentiment alone did not show the same reversal. Causality was not established.
items.attribution: Li and Wang — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Review finds modest average gains from combining clinical text and structured records
items.streamSummary: A systematic review retained 57 of 641 studies and found a reported average 6.4% improvement for LLM-enabled multimodal prediction. Heterogeneous studies and deployment limits constrain the claim.
items.attribution: Kaster et al. — npj Digital Medicine (systematic review)

items.streamTitle: Phishing texts used urgency and action cues absent from a small legitimate sample
items.streamSummary: A linguistic comparison of 106 scam texts and 16 legitimate texts found frequent urgency, authority, and link-related cues in scams. It did not test whether new warnings reduce victimization.
items.attribution: Kawabata — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: China–Japan policy comparison highlights differing responses to AI plagiarism
items.streamSummary: A document-based comparison of Chinese policy and 359 Japanese universities identified institutional silence and a Japanese 'No Copy + Exceptions' approach. It did not test which policy prevents plagiarism.
items.attribution: Zhang and Chen — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications
